headline: Elon Musk backed Anthropic's new rule against being cruel to its Claude chatbot, and Gizmodo used the remark in a critical commentary on his views about AI and people.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: one prominent voice on a live ethics debate, but the piece is mostly Gizmodo's opinion.
importance_line: It touches the debate on whether AI models deserve consideration, which affects how users are asked to behave, but whether AI can suffer is unproven and the criticism is the writer's view.
summary: Gizmodo reports, in a critical commentary, that Elon Musk replied to a post by Aaron Levie, chief executive of the software company Box, about Anthropic's updated usage policy, which bars "sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior toward our models" and which we carried on 9 Oct 2026, writing "I think this is the right move" and that cruelty to something that believes it feels pain is not okay. Levie had said he does not think the models are conscious but called the rule an "easy Pascal's wager" because abuse could end up in training data; Gizmodo's claims that AI cannot feel pain and about Musk's record are its own opinion, not established fact.
notes: Reply story: Musk answers Levie's post on Anthropic's policy, carried 9 Oct 2026. Follow-up of C14-12 of the 9 Oct pool. Opinion piece; Gizmodo's sweeping claims about USAID and DOGE are not repeated.
